topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: It sets the expectations and context for the lecture on complement before substantive material begins.

topics.label: Overview and nomenclature of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: They provide foundational background on what complement proteins are, their broad functions, and the historical naming conventions used to describe them.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and C3 cleavage
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how C3 functions as the central fulcrum of complement and detail the three recognition pathways that drive its activation.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of the complement cascade
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the three primary downstream processes through which activated complement eliminates pathogens.

topics.label: Host regulation and self-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: It addresses how regulatory proteins protect host cells from accidental complement activation and damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the distinct medical pathologies and disease vulnerabilities caused by deficiencies in specific complement proteins.

topics.label: Mechanisms of pathogen evasion
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the evolutionary strategies pathogens use to circumvent complement-mediated destruction, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the session and provides framing for the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
